summary: A signed primary-model obstacle on the normal-crossing surface has no greatest geometric C or D minorant.
detailedSummary: Proves the proposed obstruction on every support over every field, using G331's entire geometric comparison. Computes a stronger signed model obstacle, exact canonical ideals, pointwise convergence with uniform error1/2 in every degree, non-FG, gauge covariance and an open family of failures. Both normal components retain CE.
text:
The proposal is valid for the ACTUAL G331 geometric C/D cone over EVERY field k. Let R=k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z)/(xy), m=(x,y,z), X=V_m with ALL supports. Its finite normalization is k[x,z]_(x,z) times k[y,z]_(y,z). R is their fibre product over k[z]_(z): pairs have the same residue, and separating their two remainders reconstructs R. Component idempotents make the normalization finite and show that the conductor is exactly(x,y). The reduced quotient boundary has two source points over one target point o, with support(x,y), v_o(z)=1. G331 gives singleton fibres everywhere else.

On branch1 set f1=-1/2. On branch2 set f2=-1/2-1/(2w(y)), with 1/infinity=0. Since min(w(y),w(z))=1, w(y)>=1. Extended evaluation and reciprocal on[1,infinity] are continuous; f2 lies in[-1,-1/2]. The source functions agree at EVERY conductor fibre. The compact quotient therefore gives an actual finite continuous signed obstacle f downstairs.

Let v1 be the GENERIC branch2 monomial valuation y=z=1, killing x. For ANY proper primary ideal I, e=v_o(I) is a positive finite integer. An element attaining e has a unit denominator and a branch2 numerator with nonzero z^e coefficient in its y=0 residue. Generic monomial evaluation cannot cancel distinct monomials, so v1(I)<=e. Units give equality0. Hence every finite REAL negative primary combination obeys q(o)<=q(v1). G331's proved uniform comparison extends this to ENTIRE geometric C, including real Cartier core evaluations; taking infima in ACTUAL decreasing C-nets extends it to ENTIRE D, including bottom. Thus every geometric minorant g<=f has g(o)<=-1. Every normalized valuation on the regular second branch dominates ordinary m-order. Applying the same comparison and decreasing-limit argument gives g(w)<=g(v1)<=-1 on ALL of branch2, including arbitrary supports.

For n>=1 take the genuine primary ideal I_n=m^(2n)+x^2m^n and h_n=-v(I_n)/(2n). Ideal sum/product identities hold on EVERY support. On branch1 h_n=max(-1,-1/2-v(x)/n); on branch2 and o it is-1. ACTUAL Bl_(I_n) carries effective Cartier E_n, and -E_n/(2n) is negative effective REAL Cartier, relatively ample, and of positive degree on EVERY contracted integral curve BEFORE taking limits. Thus h_n is a geometric-core minorant of f. At every finite-x branch1 point h_n increases to-1/2. The sole branch1 point killing x is o. The constant-1 is also a competitor. Consequently the COMPLETE raw C/D supremum is p=-1/2 on branch1 minus o, and p=-1 on branch2 including o. The upper bounds hold for every geometric competitor; the lower bounds are actual positive primary competitors. This determines the entire boundary.

Generic monomial w_r(x)=r,w_r(z)=1,w_r(y)=infinity, r>=1, converges to o on EVERY element of R: polynomial minima tend to the order of the x=0 residue, or infinity when that residue is0; all local unit denominators have value0. But p(w_r)=-1/2 and p(o)=-1. Thus p is not USC or continuous. Every D function is USC as an infimum of continuous functions. A greatest C or D minorant would equal its raw supremum, so neither exists. Equivalently a greatest minorant must dominate all h_n, equal-1/2 on finite-x points, and be<=-1 at o, contradicting USC. The USC regularization p* has p*(o)=-1/2 and p*(v1)=-1. It violates the proved geometric inequality. Although p*<=f, it cannot be declared positive.

There is a stronger finite signed PRIMARY-MODEL obstacle with exactly the same failure: J=(y)+m^2 and F=(1/2)v(J)-(3/2)v(m). On branch1 F=-1/2; on branch2 F=(1/2)min(w(y),2)-3/2, in[-1,-1/2]. F(o)=-1/2 and F(v1)=-1. It is a signed actual exceptional REAL Cartier evaluation on a common primary blowup of m and J. The same h_n are below F, and the same universal inequalities give the same raw p and no greatest C/D minorant.

For BOTH obstacles, in EVERY degree m>=1 the canonical ideal is A_m=(z^m)+x(x,z)^(ceil(m/2)-1)+y(y,z)^(m-1). On branch1 the defining condition is exactly ordinary order>=ceil(m/2), by the generic order valuation and domination by all normalized supports. On branch2 it is exactly order>=m: necessity is v1, sufficiency uses f2,F2>=-1. The common z-residue of the two component functions must then have order>=m. Separating it from the x- and y-divisible remainders proves the displayed downstairs ideal identity, including local-unit denominators. If s=v(x),t=v(z), min(s,t)=1 on branch1, its canonical profile is h_m=-min(mt,s+ceil(m/2)-1)/m. On branch2 and o it is-1.

Every h_m has an ACTUAL negative effective ample primary presentation and converges pointwise in EVERY degree to p. Nevertheless ||p-h_m||=1/2 for EVERY m: take t=1 and finite s>=m-ceil(m/2)+1 to obtain h_m=-1,p=-1/2; everywhere the difference is in[0,1/2]. The canonical algebra is not finitely generated by n1's forward implication from finite generation to a continuous rational-primary envelope. Here non-FG accompanies an independently proved failure; it does not replace the regularity argument.

The failure is stable: if ||f'-f||<epsilon<1/4, h_n-epsilon are C minorants of f'. A greatest C/D minorant would be>=-1/2-epsilon along the finite-x locus, but at o the universal inequality gives value<=-1+epsilon. USC along w_r makes these incompatible.

On the unnormalized cone, lambda=v(m), the proposed second-component obstacle is-lambda/2-lambda^2/(2v(y)), with the second summand0 at infinity; the first is-lambda/2. These are degree-one homogeneous. F is already homogeneous. Raw p is-lambda/2 on finite-x first-component points and-lambda otherwise. Exact primary transport divides by the same bounded positive denominator, preserving discontinuity and nonexistence; canonical ideals are unchanged. Completion preserves the example.

This is a genuinely NONNORMAL obstruction with nonsingleton infinite-conductor fibres. Each normal surface component has CE by n1. It contradicts neither bijective normalization transport nor reduced-curve min(f,0), where conductor fibres are singletons. Literal radial extension, products, energy and full operators remain separate. Artifacts: n2.md, n2.tex, diagnostics.py and reports/diagnostics.json. Rerun: python diagnostics.py; python deliver.py; python check_delivery.py. Finite checks are observations; the argument above covers all supports.
